title: Monotonic Social Choice Function
body_html:
Monotonic Social Choice Function

A social choice function $G$ is monotonic (in the Maskin sense, restricted to strict comparisons against the chosen winner) if a winner remains a winner whenever it is weakly pushed up in everyone's ranking: for every pair of profiles $P, Q$ and every alternative $a$, $$ G(P) = a \;\wedge\; \bigl(\forall i,\ \forall c \ne a,\ a \succ_{P_i} c \Rightarrow a \succ_{Q_i} c\bigr) \;\Rightarrow\; G(Q) = a. $$

In Lean: SocialChoice.Voting.SCF.Monotonic.

The condition only requires that strict $a$-vs-$c$ comparisons in favor of the winner persist; voters may rearrange their rankings among non-winning alternatives freely.

Monotonicity is the bridge from strategy-proofness ([[social_choice.voting.strategyproof]]) to dictatorship in the Gibbard –Satterthwaite chain: strategy-proof SCFs are monotonic ([[social_choice.voting.strategyproof_implies_monotonic]]), and monotonic unanimous SCFs with $|A| \ge 3$ are dictatorial ([[social_choice.voting.muller_satterthwaite]]).

References

  • [MSZ 21.22] Maschler, Solan, and Zamir, Game Theory, references/GameTheory.pdf. Monotonicity for SCFs.
